title: Push a swing more often, go higher?
hook: Eight equal shoves on a swing. Which rhythm builds the biggest swing?

knows: pushing a swing makes it go higher
a swing goes out and back on its own
doesNotKnow: that driving in step with the natural period (resonance) builds the motion

misconception: More frequent pushes always give a bigger swing.
objective: The learner can explain that a swing builds when each push arrives in step with its own rhythm, and that pushes out of step undo each other.

claims.text: A swing has its own rhythm, set by its length: a 2.0 s period needs a rope of 0.99 m.
claims.source: Small-angle pendulum period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g); L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2) = 9.81 x 4 / 39.48 = 0.994 m. Point-mass swing idealisation.

claims.text: Shoving every 2 s, each shove meets the swing moving forward and adds; 8 shoves reach about 26 degrees in this model.
claims.source: Damped linear oscillator theta'' = -w^2 theta - 2 z w theta' (w = pi rad/s, z = 0.01), 8 forward kicks of 4 degrees' amplitude each from rest, Euler-Cromer at dt = 1/2400 s (Demo.tsx): max 25.5 degrees. Kick size and damping are illustrative.

claims.text: Shoving every 1 s or every 3 s, every other shove hits the swing coming back and stops it, so it never passes one shove's swing of about 4 degrees.
claims.source: Same model: kicks at half-odd multiples of the period arrive at the bottom with the swing moving backward and cancel its speed; max 3.9 degrees for both rhythms. Derivation: a kick at t = T/2 or 3T/2 after the previous one meets velocity -J e^(-z w t), leaving J(1 - e^(-z w t)), near zero.

claims.text: Driving a lightly damped oscillator in step with its natural period builds a large motion (resonance); out of step, pushes partly undo each other.
claims.source: Driven damped harmonic oscillator; Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 15 (forced oscillations and resonance).

claims.text: Model: small swings, light friction, equal brief forward shoves, played 8 times faster than real time.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Played 8x fast') and in the reveal. At 26 degrees the small-angle period error is about 1%.

recall.question: A child's swing goes out and back every 3 s. To build it up fastest, how often should you push?
recall.why: Pushes add up only when each one arrives in step with the swing's own rhythm; every 1.5 s, half of them meet it coming back.
